_doc._about: Example Observation. Keys starting with _ are comments and are ignored by the reader. Only id and windows are required; every other field may be omitted when the sampler lacks it. Resource ids: gpu:<dev>, cpu, ram, disk:<dev>, link:<link id>, host.
_doc.id: free text name of the run
_doc.batch: batch size or concurrency; 1 = stages run one after another (serialized), more = resources overlap (load). Default 1
_doc.windows: repeated windows of the same steady state; 8 or more give a useful confidence interval
_doc.windows[].busy_s: resource id -> seconds the resource was busy (GPU kernels, CPU expert work, disk reads, link transfers, host scheduling)
_doc.windows[].bytes: resource id -> work moved: bytes for gpu, cpu, disk and links, tokens handled for host. bytes / busy_s is compared with expected.rates
_doc.windows[].split_s: step time split in seconds: compute, cpu_experts, expert_load_wait, transfer_wait, host
_doc.env.throttle: GPU throttle reasons seen during the run: device (gpu id), reason = thermal | power | clocks | sw
_doc.env.pcie: per GPU: link (link id, resource link:<id>), gen_current, width_current, gen_max, width_max
_doc.env.cpu_quota_cores: CPU quota in cores (cgroup or host threads)
_doc.env.cpu_other_cores: cores used by processes other than the engine
_doc.env.major_faults_per_s: major page faults per second of the engine processes
_doc.env.memory_stall_share: share of wall time some engine task stalled on memory (PSI memory.pressure some of its cgroup); omit without PSI
_doc.env.vram_other_bytes: gpu id -> VRAM bytes held by other processes
_doc.env.disk_other_read_bytes_per_s: read rate of other processes on the engine's disk
_doc.env.io_max_bytes_per_s: io.max read limit of the cgroup, null if none
_doc.env.expert_hit_rate: share of expert uses served from VRAM
_doc.env.slots_planned: VRAM expert slots the plan asked for
_doc.expected.rates: calibrated work per busy second per resource (same unit as windows[].bytes); omit expected to skip rate checks
_doc.expected.band: relative error band from the calibration anchors; a rate more than this far below expected is a fault. Default 0.1
